title: Prioritize routing order for version pinning, rollout policies, and region/tier selection
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem statement: There is ambiguity and occasional surprising behavior when requests are processed through multiple policy layers: region selection (client hint / geo-preference), customer tier routing (free/standard/enterprise), per-route rollout policies (canary/A-B) and explicit model version pinning at the API key or token level. Several customers reported traffic split inconsistencies during staged rollouts where pinned users were incorrectly routed to canary variants, and failure fallbacks that ignored regional constraints.

Goal: Define a deterministic, audited routing precedence and a set of safe defaults that preserve developer expectations (pins are respected), maintain rollout integrity (canaries receive only intended traffic), and allow regional and tier preferences to constrain candidates without accidentally overriding pins. Produce API and console changes, telemetry schema, and migration guidance for existing pinned routes.

Scope: Route-level and token/API-key level pinning, route rollout policies (percentage canary, A-B), region preference and client geo-hints, tier-based routing, model variant fallback behavior (compatible fallbacks when the primary model is unavailable). Non-goals: deep changes to underlying scheduler or kernel selection algorithm; separate initiative will handle autoscaling/burst capacity behaviors.
acceptance_criteria: Formal spec doc in Confluence describing deterministic precedence and tie-breakers (versioned)
API change spec (HTTP/SDK) for explicit pin representation and pin precedence semantics
Console UX mocks and copy explaining pin vs rollout behavior, and a way to preview routing decision for a given token/route
Engineers implement routing precedence with unit + integration tests covering pin+rollout+region+tier combinations
Telemetry events emitted for each routing decision (decision_reason, matched_policies, final_model, fallback_chain)

Sensible defaults: pins override rollouts; route-level rollout can be opted into to include pinned traffic only with explicit consent; region preference filters candidates but does not silently override explicit pins
Backward-compatibility doc and migration plan for existing pinned routes with ambiguous behavior
updates: 2026-01-12: Triage meeting (Aisha, Liam, Priya S.). Identified customer-reported incidents: 2 enterprise accounts where pinned sessions switched to canary variant after failover. Logged INVESTIGATION-211.

2026-01-15: Product + Design sync. Proposed precedence draft: 1) Explicit pin (token/api-key) 2) Route-level sticky assignment (existing session affinity) 3) Route-level rollout policy (canary/A-B) 4) Tier routing (customer plan) 5) Region preference and geo-hint. Design emphasized clear UX and an override indicator in console.

2026-01-20: Engineering architecture review with Runtime and Routing teams. Trade-offs discussed: enforcing pin as top precedence simplifies expectations but reduces canary coverage for power users; alternate option: allow an 'include_pinned_in_rollout' flag per rollout. Eng suggested emitting decision_reason for every request for auditing.
2026-01-22: PM decision: Adopt pin-as-top-precedence with an optional rollout flag 'include_pinned' (default false). Documented in spec draft. Liam to shepherd eng work. Estimated 5 points.

2026-01-28: Design provided console mockups: Add a 'Routing preview' modal on route page showing how a sample token would be resolved across region/tier/rollout scenarios. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/routing-preview (internal)

2026-02-01: ENG spike completed (ENG-XXXXX). Findings: implementing include_pinned_in_rollout requires token-level flags in routing decision path; small perf cost due to extra policy eval (benchmarked ~0.6% p99 increase under synthetic load). Runtime team ok with change if gated behind feature flag.

2026-02-03: Drafted telemetry schema for routing_decision events. Added fields: request_id, decision_reason, matched_rollout_id, is_pinned, pin_scope (token|route), matched_region, fallback_chain (comma-separated), final_model_version. Data team asked to keep event size minimal.

2026-02-05: Created initial GitHub RFC PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/1891. Assigned reviewers @runtime-team. Next: finalize API wireframes and schedule implementation sprint for Cycle 2026-W07.
